complexity_detail.description: A function call expression evaluates the postfix-expression and initializes each parameter from the corresponding argument.
How the argument reaches the callee - copy, move, or reference binding - is decided entirely by the PARAMETER's declaration, not by anything at the call site; the same call text means any of them.
Unqualified name lookup for the callee is augmented by argument-dependent lookup, so the candidate set depends on the namespaces associated with the argument types.

A user-defined conversion may be applied at the argument position when the parameter type has a non-explicit constructor from the argument type; at most one such conversion is in an implicit conversion sequence.
A braced-init-list initializer prefers an initializer_list constructor, so `std::vector<int> x{1, 2, 3}` builds a three-element vector rather than calling the (count, value) constructor.
std::vector stores its elements contiguously in storage it owns and may reallocate; its destructor destroys the elements and deallocates that storage.
std::vector's operator[] returns a reference to the element, with pos < size() as a precondition and no check.
Automatic objects are destroyed when the block exits - including via a return - with nothing written at the exit point.
A function with no noexcept-specifier is potentially-throwing, so an undeclared exception may escape any call.

The general rule is that an lvalue argument is copied into a by-value parameter; the exceptions are that an rvalue argument is moved, and that a returned or thrown local is treated as an rvalue for overload resolution first. complexity_detail.description: std::back_inserter returns an output iterator that holds a pointer to the container and appends through push_back on assignment.

The general rule is that a container's iterators and references stay valid; the exception is that vector's push_back invalidates ALL of them when reallocation occurs, so appending through an output iterator can move every existing element.
complexity_detail.citation: ISO C++20 [vector.modifiers]/ (reallocation invalidates all iterators and references)

complexity_detail.description: std::vector's default constructor constructs an empty vector and allocates nothing; its destructor destroys the elements and deallocates.
